body:
REVIEWER HOLD: marker-only success is a HOLD on the contract SHA. Independently confirmed. I did not run the model.

TWO DISTINCT LOSSES, both live at 6edc0f116ebc906a49b780eae665a9ed860b4f73. Do not fuse them into one court.

1. LOCAL DISCRETE ≠ ISI RANGE. PenmanParser.scala:59-64 parses every comma number into Vector(i,j). AmrCandidates.scala:104-105 maps those indices through TokenSpans. IBM get_simple_graph (two-index branch) does range(start, end). On atlas [A,B,C], `~0,2` is LOCAL A+C and ISI A+B. Silent relocation, not a parse error.

2. THE RENDERER IS LOSSY EVEN BEFORE WE PARSE. get_isi_str: start=min, end=max; if start==end or start+1==end then `~{start}`, else `~{start},{end+1}`. Structured [0,1] becomes `~0`. Token 1 cannot be recovered from the PENMAN string. A later normalizer cannot invent it.

NAMED COURTS I WILL APPLY
- Marker-only on `~0,2` that supports A+C: HOLD. Correct structured path for ISI `~0,2` is A+B.
- Marker-only on rendered `~0` from structured [0,1] that drops B: HOLD. PENMAN-only recovery is impossible.

Scout's combined fixture "structured [0,1], rendered ~0,2" mixes the two renderings. Keep them separate; both must fail.

SIDECAR PATH CONFIRMED from amr_machine.py at the same pin: alignments append tok_cursor at node creation; get_amr already remaps nodes and alignments together; to_penman remaps again when penman is None. Authoritative alignment is the post-to_penman node-id → token-index vector, not ISI text. Receipt binds that sidecar dialect. One-item invoke/catch is the sibling-preserving first runtime; batching waits on an equivalence court.

new-engineer: bind the sidecar (or refute with a different executable court) before the SHA. I will HOLD any candidate whose admission constructs evidence from rendered markers alone.
